overview.headline: Newton's laws explain inertia, force and action reaction in flight

keyPoints.point: An object remains at rest or in motion unless an unbalanced force acts on it.
keyPoints.quote: An object at rest remains at rest, and an object in motion remains in motion

keyPoints.point: Acceleration depends on the mass and amount of force applied to an object.
keyPoints.quote: The acceleration of an object depends on the mass of the object and the amount of force applied.

keyPoints.point: When one object exerts a force, the second object exerts an equal and opposite reaction.
keyPoints.quote: Whenever one object exerts a force on a second object, the second object exerts an equal and opposite force on the first.

keyPoints.point: Inertia is the tendency to resist changes in motion when net forces cancel.
keyPoints.quote: This tendency to resist changes in a state of motion is inertia.

keyTerms.gloss: tendency to resist changes in motion for an object at rest or in motion
keyTerms.quote: This tendency to resist changes in a state of motion is inertia.

keyTerms.gloss: change in velocity over time determined by applied force and mass
keyTerms.quote: The acceleration of an object depends on the mass of the object and the amount of force applied.

keyTerms.gloss: mass times velocity that defines change in momentum over time
keyTerms.quote: Momentum is defined to be the mass m of an object times its velocity V.

keyTerms.gloss: vector that has both magnitude and direction such as velocity and force
keyTerms.quote: Scientists and mathematicians call this a vector quantity.

keyTerms.gloss: total force acting on an object after external forces cancel each other
keyTerms.quote: If all the external forces cancel each other out, then there is no net force acting on the object.
